'''Daniel I-Chyau Wang''' ({{lang-zh|c=王義翹|p=Wáng Yìqiào}}；March 12, 1936 &ndash; August 29, 2020) was a Chinese-American chemical engineer. He was an [[Institute Professor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He was known for founding the MIT Biotechnology Process Engineering Center and the expansion of the field of biochemical engineering.<ref name="MIT Bio">{{cite news |last1=Trafton |first1=Anne |date=2 September 2020 |title=Daniel Wang, Institute Professor and pioneer in biochemical engineering, dies at 84 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2020/daniel-wang-professor-dies-0902 |access-date=22 June 2023 |work=[[MIT News]] |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |language=en |agency=MIT News Office}}</ref><ref name="NAE Tribute">{{cite web |title=Dr. Daniel I. C. Wang |url=https://www.nae.edu/28402/Dr-Daniel-I-C-Wang |website=NAE Website |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Bowker">{{cite book|title=American men & women of science: a biographical directory of today's leaders in physical, biological and related sciences|author=R.R. Bowker company|date=1992|publisher=Bowker|isbn=9780835230810|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1P4pKXCQ62kC|accessdate=2014-10-04}}</ref>

==Career==
Wang received his [[B.S.]] (1959) and [[M.S.]] (1961) from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), and Ph.D. from in chemical engineering from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1963 working with [[Arthur E. Humphrey]] on high‐temperature short‐time sterilization.

Wang joined the MIT faculty in 1965 as a member of the department of Nutrition and Food Science. In 1995, he was named an [[Institute Professor]]. While at MIT, he established joint programs with the [[National University of Singapore]] which would ultimately become a part of the  Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology (SMART) Centre. His research on fermentation, monitoring and control of bioprocesses, renewable resource utilization, enzyme technology, product recovery and purification, protein aggregation and refolding, and mammalian cell cultures made him a pioneer in biochemical and biological engineering.<ref name="BTBE Obituary">{{cite journal |last1=Afeyan |first1=Noubar B. |last2=Cooney |first2=Charles L. |title=Professor Daniel I.C. Wang: A Legacy of Education, Innovation, Publication, and Leadership |journal=Biotechnology and Bioengineering |date=December 2020 |volume=117 |issue=12 |pages=3615–3627 |doi=10.1002/bit.27644|pmid=33616929 |hdl=1721.1/141250.2 |s2cid=229935755 |hdl-access=free |pmc=7839494 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Drew |first1=Stephen W. |title=DANIEL I.C. WANG 1936-2020 |journal=Memorial Tributes |volume=24 |url=https://www.nae.edu/280955/DANIEL-IC-WANG-19362020 |publisher=National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>

Wang was a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]],<ref name="NAE Tribute"/> the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Daniel I-Chyau Wang |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/daniel-i-chyau-wang |access-date=16 September 2023 |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> and [[Academia Sinica]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Daniel I.-C. Wang |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=188 |access-date=16 September 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref> He co-authored five books and more than 250 papers in professional journals. He was a co-founder of the Society for Biological Engineering of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ellis |first1=Gordon |title=MIT's Daniel I. C. Wang, Co-founder of AIChE's Society for Biological Engineering, Dies at 84 |url=https://www.aiche.org/chenected/2020/09/mits-daniel-i-c-wang-co-founder-aiches-society-biological-engineering-dies-84 |publisher=American Institute of Chemical Engineers |access-date=September 17, 2023 |date=September 8, 2020}}</ref> In 2019, the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] established the D.I.C. Wang Award for Excellence in Biochemical Engineering in his honor.<ref name="MIT Bio" /><ref name="NAE Tribute" />
